intro: Middle Brother National Park lies west of Kendall on the New South Wales north coast, a hill of tall blackbutt forest and rainforest. Off Bird Tree Road, the Bird Tree day-use area has a loop walk past two of the biggest blackbutts in the state, the Bird Tree and Benaroon. A reader sent us the photograph of a giant there, with figures that match the Bird Tree's. Entry is free.

trees.story:
A reader sent this blackbutt with a GPS fix taken beside Bird Tree Road, inside Middle Brother National Park, west of Kendall on the New South Wales north coast, and gave it a girth of 11 metres and an age of about 300 years.

Those are the figures the New South Wales government gives for the Bird Tree, one of two blackbutts here it calls among the biggest in the state: 69 metres high and 11 metres round. The National Trust's tree register estimates the Bird Tree at about 300 years. The other giant on the same loop walk, Benaroon, is rated the largest blackbutt in Australia, with a girth of 15 metres. The reader did not name their tree, so this page gives the figures and leaves the name to whoever stands there next.

The photograph is taken from the foot of the trunk, looking up. A timber boardwalk runs right around the base, which flares out like a buttressed column and carries a small dark hollow low on one side. Above, the grey trunk rises clean and straight through a canopy of rainforest, palms and ferns, and only branches far overhead, where the crown is lost in mist.

Scientists quoted by the state think both giants were already growing before Europeans reached Australia. If you know which of the two this is, tell us here.
trees.how_to_recognise: A huge pale-barked eucalypt ringed by a timber boardwalk, its base flaring out like a buttressed column with a small dark hollow low on one side, the trunk rising straight and unbranched far into the rainforest canopy.
trees.verify_notes: 2026-11-16 session (Hidde asked for the open reader inbox): sent by a reader through the app with a GPS fix (sighting 657dd07e), species Blackbutt, girth 1100 cm, age 300. Photograph viewed: the whole trunk from its foot on a boardwalk up into the crown, daylight, colour. Published under the reader-found rule. OpenStreetMap reverse lookup puts the fix on Bird Tree Road, Middle Brother. The reader's girth and age match the NSW Government (Bird Tree 69 m, girth 11 m; Benaroon girth 15 m) and the National Trust register (Bird Tree about 300 years), but no source places either tree at this fix, so the page does not claim the name. corroborate.py: no register entry within 100 m. The reader's two further photographs show a different, fire-hollowed trunk without the boardwalk, with a person in front; not published.
trees.access: Middle Brother National Park, free entry. The Bird Tree day-use area has a loop walk past the two giant blackbutts; the state says it does not cater for people with access needs.
